linkedin.hook: Curve showed us why pooled risk models fail institutional capital.
linkedin.copy:
When a founder borrows nine figures against their own governance token across shared liquidity pools, every depositor inherits that liquidation profile. Curve demonstrated that pooled debt models eventually depend on off-market OTC bailouts instead of programmatic execution. For institutions, this means base yields are silently underwriting catastrophic contagion risk.

The underlying failure is monolithic state design. When collateral pools share contract memory, bad debt forces haircut socialization or complete withdrawal freezes. Real isolation requires separating credit state at the smart contract level. Vanna uses independent SmartAccount sandboxes on Stellar Soroban. If a borrower goes underwater, the bad debt remains locked in their specific account instance without contaminating other liquidity providers.

Solvency enforcement also requires predictable execution rails. With a 1.10x Health Factor floor, deterministic ~320ms Mercury indexer latency, and fixed 0.00014 XLM transaction overhead, liquidations clear onchain without gas wars or front-running cascades. You can deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance to inspect the state isolation model directly.

Institutional architecture is documented at test.stellar.vanna.finance

reddit.hook: Why shared-pool lending protocols still require OTC bailouts, and how sandbox isolation changes the mechanics
reddit.copy:
The Curve liquidation episode confirmed an architectural flaw that DeFi has ignored for years: pooled lending models force every participant to underwrite systemic counterparty risk.

In standard pooled architectures like Aave or Curve-era lending, all collateral sits in shared pool contracts. When a massive position approaches liquidation, the debt size exceeds available onchain market depth. Liquidators cannot clear the position without causing severe slippage, leaving protocols with two bad choices: let bad debt accrue directly to liquidity providers, or negotiate private OTC agreements with friendly balance sheets to absorb the collateral at a discount.

This is a smart contract design choice, not an inevitable market dynamic.

Instead of a monolithic liquidity bucket, Vanna isolates each borrower position into its own SmartAccount sandbox on Stellar Soroban. Collateral and borrow state exist only inside that specific contract instance. If a borrower over-leverages, the risk envelope is strictly bounded to that sandbox. Contagion cannot spill into unrelated liquidity pools, eliminating the need to socialize losses across the protocol.

Liquidation efficiency depends heavily on indexing and execution speed. Vanna pairs isolated sandboxes with a strict 1.10x Health Factor floor. State reads operate against the Mercury indexer at roughly ~320ms latency, giving liquidators accurate pricing before deep underwater cascades develop. Because Soroban execution costs average 0.00014 XLM with deterministic fees, liquidators do not need to bid up priority gas auctions to execute time-critical unwinds.

If you want to review the contract interactions and test how isolated account instances handle debt state under volatility, our contracts are live on testnet.

Deployment workflow:
1. Fund a testnet account using the Stellar Friendbot.
2. Connect your signer to test.stellar.vanna.finance.
3. Deploy your SmartAccount sandbox instance and verify the isolated state parameters directly on the Soroban RPC.

Disclosure: I work on the core engineering team at Vanna Protocol.
